roles.producer: Builds AI models where the model is the product or a core asset, or where the model is distributed to others (API, open weights, embedded in products).
roles.consumer: Uses AI. Not a lower tier of producer: a different question set. Fine-tuning an existing model for own use (internal domain model, PoC) is consumer with the self_hosted modifier; a company whose product is a tuned model that others receive is a producer.

capability.base: LLM use with no access beyond the prompt.
capability.rag: The LLM reads org data through retrieval (RAG, knowledge graph).
capability.mcp: The LLM has tools through MCP or similar: it can read, write and take actions.
capability.agentic: Operates with minimal human oversight; autonomous multi-step work.
capability.note: Each rung includes the ones below. A question's capability is the lowest rung at which it applies. Classic ML and vision models are out of scope.

scope_tags.internal: Day-to-day business processes; output stays inside the org.
scope_tags.code_generation: AI builds or maintains business applications; the output is a persistent executable artifact (insecure code, hallucinated dependencies, licensing, secrets, review gates).
scope_tags.customer_facing: AI inside an app, or output reaching customers or end users, including calling a SaaS LLM API from the org's own app.
scope_tags.third_party_embedded: AI bundled in a tool the org uses (ITSM, ticketing, RPA with a built-in LLM); less control, supply-chain focus.
scope_tags.note: An empty list means the question applies to all usage contexts.

modifiers.builds_on_base_model: Producer builds on an existing base model and inherits upstream risk (licence, inherited bias or safety gaps, base-model change or withdrawal).
modifiers.self_hosted: The org hosts the model or its infrastructure itself, so responsibility shifts from the provider to the org.
modifiers.poc: A proof of concept or experiment, often with real data, a larger exposure surface and fewer checks.
modifiers.unsanctioned_use: Shadow AI: use of AI tools nobody approved.

topics.governance: Oversight, accountability, inventory, impact, third parties and release decisions.
topics.data_model: Data and model protection: RAG and knowledge-graph content, weights, fine-tuned models and prompts are assets.
topics.infra: Protecting where sensitive things are hosted; wording differs for SaaS vs self-hosted.
topics.reliability: Tuning, harness, guardrails, testing; wrong or hostile inputs and outputs, from normal model behaviour or from attack.
topics.ai_access: AI as a new identity with permissions (agents, MCP, RAG): what data it can reach, what it can do, whose permissions it uses, whether a human approves actions.

items.outcome: Intended purpose, potentially beneficial uses, context-specific laws, norms and expectations, and prospective settings in which the AI system will be deployed are understood and documented. Considerations include: specific set or types of users along with their expectations; potential positive and negative impacts of system uses to individuals, communities, organizations, society, and the planet; assumptions and related limitations about AI system purposes; uses and risks across the development or product AI lifecycle; TEVV and system metrics.
suggested_actions: Maintain awareness of industry, technical, and applicable legal standards.
Examine trustworthiness of AI system design and consider, non-AI solutions
Consider intended AI system design tasks along with unanticipated purposes in collaboration with human factors and socio-technical domain experts.
Define and document the task, purpose, minimum functionality, and benefits of the AI system to inform considerations about whether the utility of the project or its lack of.
Identify whether there are non-AI or non-technology alternatives that will lead to more trustworthy outcomes.

Examine how changes in system performance affect downstream events such as decision-making (e.g: changes in an AI model objective function create what types of impacts in how many candidates do/do not get a job interview).
Determine actions to map and track post-decommissioning stages of AI deployment and potential negative or positive impacts to individuals, groups and communities.
Determine the end user and organizational requirements, including business and technical requirements.
Determine and delineate the expected and acceptable AI system context of use, including:
potential positive and negative impacts to individuals, groups, communities, organizations, and society

Perform context analysis related to time frame, safety concerns, geographic area, physical environment, ecosystems, social environment, and cultural norms within the intended setting (or conditions that closely approximate the intended setting.
Gain and maintain awareness about evaluating scientific claims related to AI system performance and benefits before launching into system design.
Identify human-AI interaction and/or roles, such as whether the application will support or replace human decision making.
Plan for risks related to human-AI configurations, and document requirements, roles, and responsibilities for human oversight of deployed systems.

categories.covers: Intended purpose and context of each AI use, who is affected, benefits and harms, impact assessment, fairness and bias in the way outputs are used, human oversight and review of outputs, transparency to users.
